runs.market_commentary:
Asian markets closed mixed on Thursday, with the Nikkei 225 gaining 128 points (+0.20%) to close at 65,270 as Japanese equities benefited from yen weakness and positive global risk sentiment tied to AI-sector momentum. Broader Asia-Pacific sentiment was cautious ahead of key US inflation data, with markets assessing renewed Middle East hostilities that have pushed Brent crude above $102/bbl and Treasury yields to fresh 3-year highs above 4.85%.

European markets opened under pressure with the DAX slipping 10 points to 25,566 and the FTSE 100 falling 41 points to 10,628, as investors awaited the ECB's rate decision and Lagarde's press conference. The ECB was expected to signal a pause while providing updated staff forecasts; higher oil prices are complicating the inflation outlook and pushing back against dovish repricing. Treasury bear-steepening spillover weighed on euro area sovereigns, with BTP-Bund spreads widening modestly.

US pre-market futures are mixed heading into the Thursday session: Dow futures +125 pts (+0.24%) at 52,550, S&P 500 futures +6.25 pts (+0.09%) at 7,650, and Nasdaq 100 futures -63.50 pts (-0.21%) at 29,385. The divergence reflects sector rotation — Meta's JPMorgan upgrade and Apple's foldable iPhone momentum are supporting large-cap tech sentiment while semiconductor names face cooling sentiment. PPI data came in largely in-line this morning, keeping Friday's CPI as the pivotal macro event. The Fed meeting next week remains a coin flip, and with the 10-year yield above 4.85%, duration remains the primary cross-asset risk. Oil's geopolitical premium from US-Iran tensions is acting as a tax on risk assets while supporting energy stocks.

ideas.catalyst: JPMorgan upgraded META to Overweight from Neutral, raising its price target from $640 to $820, citing meaningful upside potential as Meta rolls out AI models and products across its family of apps.
ideas.thesis: Meta's investment in AI infrastructure is now translating into measurable ad-targeting improvements and new product categories including AI assistants and glasses, creating a compounding revenue growth vector that current consensus estimates do not fully capture. The JPMorgan upgrade marks a notable institutional inflection point, likely to prompt buy-side re-rating and updated sell-side models in the coming weeks.
ideas.key_risk: Regulatory action in the EU or US targeting AI data usage could constrain ad personalization, and any macro-driven ad spending pullback would compress near-term revenue guidance.

sources.label: Yahoo Finance – Thursday Top Analyst Calls

ideas.catalyst: Apple unveiled its first-ever foldable iPhone at its Sept 9 product event, adding a premium form factor to its lineup and driving pre-market gains of approximately 1%.
ideas.thesis: The foldable iPhone opens a high-ASP segment Apple can own outright, extending the upgrade cycle and boosting Services attach rates on a new device category with no prior Apple install base. Historical iPhone launch cycles tend to sustain 4-8 weeks of positive earnings estimate revision momentum as carrier partners and analysts update unit projections.
ideas.key_risk: Early consumer reviews citing durability or hinge reliability issues could suppress initial orders and trigger negative analyst revisions before the product ships.

ideas.catalyst: COO tumbled 18.1% after a disappointing strategic review, slashed full-year financial guidance, a revenue miss, and a wave of analyst downgrades hitting simultaneously.
ideas.thesis: The combination of a failed strategic review, guidance cut, and revenue miss strips away the three pillars of COO's valuation premium — growth visibility, strategic optionality, and sell-side support — leaving shares facing further de-rating as price targets are reset lower. Multiple downgrades on the same day signal a broad consensus shift, and the initial 18% drop rarely represents the full correction when guidance resets are this material.
ideas.key_risk: An unsolicited M&A approach or activist accumulation could trigger a sharp short-covering rally, particularly given the sudden valuation reset.

ideas.catalyst: AeroVironment reported Q1 EPS of $0.59 vs. the $0.25 consensus estimate (136% beat) and revenue of $480.5M vs. $456.2M estimate, reflecting surging demand for tactical unmanned systems.
ideas.thesis: AVAV's 136% earnings beat signals that DoD procurement of loitering munitions and tactical drones is accelerating well beyond what consensus models assumed, driven by lessons from ongoing global conflicts. As allies expand their own tactical drone programs and US inventories need replenishment, AVAV's position as the dominant supplier creates multi-year visibility at above-consensus ASPs.
ideas.key_risk: Congressional continuing resolutions or delays in the defense appropriations bill could slow near-term contract awards and compress quarterly booking cadence.

ideas.catalyst: Morgan Stanley upgraded DT Midstream to Overweight from Equal Weight with a $170 price target, citing improving contracted revenue visibility.
ideas.thesis: Midstream natural gas infrastructure is benefiting from two secular tailwinds simultaneously: surging LNG export capacity and growing natural gas demand from AI data centers, both of which increase throughput utilization on DTM's gathering and processing assets in premium Appalachian and Haynesville basins. The Morgan Stanley upgrade reflects confidence in DTM's ability to grow fee-based EBITDA with minimal commodity price exposure.
ideas.key_risk: Sustained natural gas price weakness or a regulatory reversal on LNG export approvals could reduce shipper incentives to expand volumes on DTM's infrastructure.

ideas.catalyst: US-Iran tensions remain elevated keeping Brent above $102/bbl while OPEC cut production by 640,000 bpd month-on-month to 19.71 million bpd.
ideas.thesis: The convergence of OPEC supply cuts and geopolitical risk premium from US-Iran tensions creates a supply shortfall entering Q4 when seasonal demand historically strengthens; Brent has a clear technical path to test $110 if diplomatic talks deteriorate further. Treasury bear-steepening also historically correlates with oil outperformance as real asset demand rises.
ideas.key_risk: Any diplomatic breakthrough between the US and Iran or a surprise OPEC+ quota increase could reverse the geopolitical premium swiftly and sharply.

sources.label: FXStreet – ECB and US PPI Sept 10

ideas.catalyst: Geopolitical tensions (US/Iran), tomorrow's CPI report, and a coin-flip Fed meeting next week support gold demand as a hedge against multiple macro outcomes.
ideas.thesis: Gold is being supported by a trifecta of elevated geopolitical risk, unresolved inflation uncertainty ahead of the CPI print, and a Federal Reserve that faces its most binary policy decision in three years; this multi-factor bid tends to be more durable than single-catalyst rallies. Even with 10-year yields at 4.85%, the real rate sensitivity is partially offset by safe-haven and central bank reserve demand.
ideas.key_risk: A materially cooler CPI print Friday could reduce inflation fears, and a hawkish-surprise Fed next week could pressure gold through a higher real rate channel.

sources.label: FXStreet – ECB and US PPI Sept 10

ideas.catalyst: 10-year Treasury yields climbed to 3-year highs above 4.85% driven by elevated oil prices, sticky inflation, and markets pricing a coin-flip Fed, extending the bear steepening trend.
ideas.thesis: The bear steepening reflects persistent inflationary pressure from $102+ Brent crude, an elevated US fiscal supply calendar, and a Federal Reserve that is not pre-committing to cuts — all of which are structurally negative for long-duration Treasuries. The path of least resistance for 10-year yields is higher until the CPI/FOMC sequence resolves, and TLT's duration (~17 years) makes it acutely sensitive to yield moves.
ideas.key_risk: A significantly weaker CPI print tomorrow or a surprise dovish tilt from the Fed next week could trigger a violent short-covering rally in long-duration Treasuries.

ideas.catalyst: Evercore downgraded CHWY to In Line from Outperform after noting that organic growth has decelerated to 5.7%, well below the double-digit rates that justified the premium multiple.
ideas.thesis: Chewy's bull thesis relied on the durable spending of pandemic-era pet adopters, but sub-6% organic growth signals the cohort has fully matured and new customer acquisition is failing to fill the gap — a structural shift that will compress the growth premium embedded in valuation. The Evercore downgrade is likely the first of several as sell-side analysts revisit long-term growth assumptions.
ideas.key_risk: A strategic announcement such as international expansion, a new product category launch, or acquisition by a larger retailer could re-rate shares sharply higher from a de-rated base.

ideas.catalyst: Wells Fargo upgraded YUM to Overweight from Equal Weight, raising the price target to $175 from $165, citing improved unit economics and franchise fee growth visibility.
ideas.thesis: Yum! Brands is a beneficiary of the consumer trade-down dynamic as inflationary pressure pushes spending toward quick-service restaurants, while its international franchise model — particularly KFC and Pizza Hut in Asia/EM — provides structural unit count growth with limited capex intensity. The Wells Fargo upgrade signals improving conviction in same-store sales recovery and international royalty growth.
ideas.key_risk: Persistent food and labor cost inflation in franchisee P&Ls could erode unit economics faster than same-store sales growth can offset, putting franchise renewals at risk.

deals.headline: WaFd Inc. enters $3.9B reverse merger with EverBank Financial Corp.
deals.description: WaFd, Inc., the Seattle-based bank holding company, entered into a $3.9 billion reverse merger transaction with EverBank Financial Corp. on September 8, 2026, creating a combined institution with significantly expanded deposit franchises and commercial lending capabilities. The combined entity will operate under the EverBank brand given its larger national consumer reach, while WaFd shareholders receive a premium to recent trading levels.

deals.headline: PayTabs acquires Amazon Payment Services MENA for $100M
deals.description: Saudi Arabia-based PayTabs Group announced the acquisition of Amazon Payment Services' Middle East and North Africa operations for $100 million, expanding its digital payments infrastructure across the region. The deal gives PayTabs Amazon's established merchant network and payment processing technology across the MENA corridor, accelerating PayTabs' path to profitability in advance of a planned regional IPO.

deals.headline: Anthropic IPO filing delayed to late-September; roadshow set for mid-October
deals.description: Reuters reported that Anthropic has delayed its S-1 filing to late September 2026, with the investor roadshow now expected to begin in mid-October at the earliest and the IPO date planned for late October, citing market conditions and ongoing regulatory review of its core AI models. The delay comes as Anthropic navigates investor scrutiny over AI safety disclosures and pricing of its enterprise API contracts, which are key to its growth narrative.

deals.headline: Major Novartis shareholder launches board overhaul campaign to improve corporate governance
deals.description: Reuters reported that a major Novartis shareholder is calling for a comprehensive overhaul of the company's board of directors to improve corporate governance, pushing for new independent directors with stronger capital allocation discipline. The campaign sent Novartis shares nearly 2% higher in pre-market trading as investors anticipate increased pressure on management to streamline the portfolio and improve return on invested capital.

deals.headline: Macy's Q2 revenue beat and raised FY2026 guidance on comp sales and EPS
deals.description: Macy's reported Q2 adjusted EPS of $0.63 vs. the $0.37 analyst consensus and net sales of $4.87B vs. $4.81B estimates, with management raising full-year net sales, comparable sales, and earnings-per-share guidance — indicating the department store's turnaround strategy is gaining traction. Despite the strong results, shares dipped 1.6% pre-market as investors weigh the raised guidance against ongoing structural headwinds in brick-and-mortar retail and a tougher consumer spending backdrop.

key_events.headline: US August PPI released in-line with expectations
key_events.impact: Producer prices rose on both monthly and yearly basis largely in line with consensus, providing a neutral setup for tomorrow's more-watched CPI report and keeping Fed rate path uncertainty intact.

key_events.headline: US August CPI due Friday, September 11 — pivotal for Fed
key_events.impact: Both CPI and PPI would need to miss consensus on core measures to materially shift FOMC expectations; the September meeting is currently priced as a coin flip between hold and a 25bp cut.

key_events.headline: ECB rate decision today with Lagarde press conference
key_events.impact: ECB expected to provide updated staff forecasts; Lagarde's guidance on willingness to tighten further will be closely watched given elevated oil prices complicating the inflation outlook.

key_events.headline: FOMC meeting September 16-17 — coin flip on rate move
key_events.impact: Fed decision next week remains the dominant macro event for equities and rates; a surprise cut would be bullish for equities and crush TLT shorts, while a hold would support the bearish duration thesis.

key_events.headline: US-Iran tensions push Brent crude above $102/bbl
key_events.impact: Elevated geopolitical risk is acting as a tax on global risk appetite while simultaneously supporting energy stocks and gold; sustained oil above $100 keeps inflation elevated and complicates central bank easing.

key_events.headline: OPEC cuts production 640,000 bpd to 19.71 million bpd
key_events.impact: OPEC's production cut tightens supply at a time of elevated geopolitical risk, underpinning the oil price floor and supporting energy sector earnings revisions higher into Q4.
